messages:
Nina P.: Anyone able to help? Trying to get redwoodctl installed for a new Windows laptop (Windows 11 Pro) and the MSI fails with a weird PowerShell error during post-install: 

Install log excerpt:
```
Running custom action CA_ConfigurePath
PowerShell script returned error code 5
Could not set PATH: Access is denied
```

I ran the installer as admin and it still chokes. Also the desktop shortcut opens the app but `redwoodctl --version` returns `permission denied` unless I open an elevated shell.

Carlos G.: Windows installer should not require elevated shell for normal users. Which MSI did you download? x86_64? Our CI produces both x86_64 and arm64 MSIs. If the MSI writes to HKLM it may need admin. Can you paste `Get-ExecutionPolicy` and the MSI file name?

Nina P.: MSI: redwoodctl-0.9.3-windows-amd64.msi. ExecutionPolicy is `RemoteSigned`. I noticed the installer tries to create a directory under `C:/Program Files/Redwood` and then add to system PATH via `Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Environment' -Name Path -Value (...)` which fails if your account is not admin even if the installer UI ran as admin (weird).

Liam O.: There's an MSI bootstrapper bug where the installer elevates the UI but the custom action runs under the invoking user. Short term workaround: 1) Run an elevated PowerShell prompt and install via `msiexec /i redwoodctl-0.9.3-windows-amd64.msi /qn` or 2) let the installer finish and then manually add `C:\Program Files\Redwood` to PATH in System settings. I'll open a fix to ensure the custom action uses `msiDeferred` with elevated privileges.

Nina P.: Workaround worked. Also FYI the installer wrote `C:\Users\Public\redwood\updates\last` with a copy of the binary that had world-readable ACLs. Not ideal.

Carlos G.: Thank you, that's a security concern. We should ensure update artifacts use per-user appdata and 0600-ish perms. Filing an issue for that.

infra-bot: Reminder: security triage today at 15:00 UTC.

Liam O.: On a related note, we've had multiple reports where `redwoodctl login` appears to attach tokens to the wrong profile when users have migrated config files between OSes. The underlying cause is that TOML parser normalizes line endings and table order differently, so our matching logic only compares `name` and picks the first match. Suggestion: use a deterministic profile key (uuid) on create and preserve it during import/migrate, fall back to name+endpoint but warn on duplicates.

Carlos G.: Agreed. Also the `redwoodctl config migrate` command should detect potential duplicates and prompt users to choose which one to keep. For non-interactive flows, add `--strategy=merge|keep-first|keep-last`.

Nina P.: Another pain: when doing local development with `redwoodctl dev --local --proxy http://localhost:9090`, the CLI launches the dev server but subsequent `redwoodctl login --profile local-test` attempts to do browser SSO and fails because the dev server is bound to 127.0.0.1 only. It times out waiting for a callback. Would love `--callback-host` or a `--headless` flag to provide the callback URL and token directly.

Liam O.: We already have `--callback-url` flag in the auth flow but it's not exposed in the older packaged binaries. I'll backport a `--no-browser --callback-url` pair to the next patch release. For CI, prefer `redwoodctl login --token-file` as a deterministic flow.

Carlos G.: Also noticed token rotation behavior: when a token is refreshed via SSO, the CLI keeps the old token in `~/.redwood/.token_history` for rollback but the history file is plain JSON with timestamps and tokens. We should encrypt or at least set perms to 0600 and rotate to a secure store on supported platforms (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, gnome-keyring). Filing enhancement.

Nina P.: Filed issue #2502: "windows-msi: elevation for custom actions, updater artifacts perms, profile keying, and headless callbacks" with logs and repro steps. Workaround summary in the issue: run MSI elevated, add PATH manually if needed, set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG to an isolated file for CI, and use `--token-file` in non-interactive flows.

redwoodctl-bot: New issue created: #2502 "windows-msi: elevation for custom actions, updater artifacts perms, profile keying, and headless callbacks" by Nina P. https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/2502

Liam O.: I'll pick up the MSI custom action fix and the token storage perms change. Carlos, can you own the profile keying migration? I'll coordinate the backport for `--no-browser`.

Carlos G.: Yup, taking profile keying + migrate strategy flags.

Nina P.: Thanks all, that saved me a lot of time. I'll add the MSI elevated install note to the Windows onboarding doc and call out the token history file perms.
